route: scripted (procedural Blender geometry; no provider generation; face art reused from the P5-T6 UI atlas)

texturesSampled: ui/dice-d6 (shared UI atlas page, resident for the UI)
ui/dice-d6-glow (shared UI atlas glow page, the face emissive map)

lods: LOD0 only: a 40 mm die stays within the 1,500-triangle dice budget (DICE_LIMITS), so a LOD chain saves nothing measurable
bake: none: face art is the shared atlas page and brass is a factor (or the shared brass-polished set), so nothing is baked

frame.convention: src/dice/faces.ts die-local frame; identity orientation = DicePresenter's
frame.uv: TEXCOORD_0 is glTF (v down); loadDice flips v once so face UVs are in the UI atlas's bottom-left texture space

materialsUsed: factor-only polished brass named after the approved P4-T3 brass-polished set (bindable at runtime); the face slot samples the shared P5-T6 UI atlas page
license: Original work generated in Blender from a checked-in script; face art and style reference from Paul's paid Higgsfield plan (Terms of Use 4.4)

checks: face table (GLB extras and manifest) equals faces.ts and content/dice.ts
reimport gate (face-up UVs in the atlas cell, no mirrored UVs, Blender reimport)

approvals.notes: validate-generated-assets verdict is reported to the orchestrator, not self-recorded
original procedural geometry; face art from the P5-T6 atlas (its own provenance)
Paul approves the in-engine look (docs/blender-kit-project.md ruling 3)
blender-kit-pieces requires an independent >= 80/100 score; unscored means unaccepted

independentScore.scale: 0-100 visual fidelity to the art direction
independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the asset)

rubric.note: Up 1 from 25. The rounded brass cube with a raised frame still matches the proportions of L-board-1 panel 4, and the faces now sit in a visible well. On the right die in p5-dice-brass-d6.jpg a scan at y=300 drops from relL 0.155 on the frame to 0.052 within 3 px (x 521 to 524) into a shadowed wall before reaching walnut, where the last score saw a nearly flush step over 10 px. The new front brass lip carries a rolled highlight that peaks at relL 0.74 (x=600, y 384 to 391). Points are still lost because the lit inner wall reads pale instead of as panel 4's dark bevel. At x=620, y 251 to 260 the back wall is a grey-mauve band (#847069, S 0.20, relL about 0.17), and the same low-saturation band appears on 4 of the 6 lineup dice (105 to 257 px each, median #76655B to #8E7568). The pips are meant to be recessed cups but do not read as cups at this framing, as the signature note measures.

Up 1 from 18. The new glow spill is real and measurable. Around the right die's centre pip (centroid 606,307, 35 x 24 px) the ring just outside the disc (normalised radius 1.05 to 1.2) measures #825B39, relL 0.125, and the next ring (1.2 to 1.4) 0.102, against walnut at p50 0.066 and p90 0.090. The spill is warm (S 0.56), so the pips now light the face as in panel 4, which they did not at the last score (0.098, inside the grain range). The pip cups do not read. Across the disc edge (radius 0.95 to 1.05) the minimum relL is 0.127 and the median 0.49, so there is no dark rim and each pip is still a flat lit disc. The pip colour remains cream rather than candle amber. The median pip is #E5C59B (H34, S 0.32), the core #E7CCA9 (S 0.27) and the brightest 1% #EED3A9 (S 0.29), up only slightly from S 0.28 and against #F3BE65 (S 0.58) and the reference core #FFD848 (S 0.72). Pip saturation never exceeds 0.46 on any face. Brass body, walnut faces, the new brass lip and the correct pip layouts are all present.

Unchanged at 12. The walnut grain is still painterly and strong. The brass is still uniform, with no edge wear, cavity darkening or value breakup. Under the previous score's hue mask (H38 to 60, S above 0.3) right-die brass relL runs p10 0.117, p50 0.153, p90 0.235 and the left die 0.107, 0.123 and 0.182, which is the same narrow band as before (0.143 to 0.240). Only the top 1% got brighter (p99 0.68), from the new rolled front lip. A stricter S above 0.45 mask gives the same picture (p10 0.117, p90 0.202). The new pale grey-mauve inner wall reads as a separate grey material rather than brass or shadowed wood, which slightly weakens the material read of the well.

Unchanged at 10. The walnut is on target: top faces #61412E and #5F402E, front faces #5A3A28 and #593A27, and the six lineup dice #5B3D2B to #6B4A32, against the bible's #583C26. The brass moved sideways rather than toward the palette. The hue-masked median is #85692E (H41, S 0.65, V 0.52), more saturated than the last score's #826F48 (S 0.45) but no brighter, against polished brass #DEC16A (H45, S 0.52, V 0.87) and the reference's lit brass #EEB249. It reads as mustard-olive rather than polished brass. The pip hue is right (H34 against candle amber H37) but saturation is about half (S 0.32 against 0.58). The grey-mauve wall (S 0.20) is an off-palette note. The value structure of light frame, dark face and bright pips is correct.

Up 1 from 8. Pip-to-walnut contrast (median pip against median walnut, WCAG) measures 5.55:1 and 6.11:1 on the right die's top and front faces and 5.66:1 and 6.15:1 on the left die, up from 4.9 to 5.5:1. The six lineup dice measure 4.75 to 5.90:1, up from 4.6 to 4.9:1, and all clear 4.5:1. The pips are countable at a glance at both framings (the centre pip spans 35 px in the closeup), and the new halo helps them read in dim light. This is still below the reference's roughly 10:1, and the evidence is desktop only.

topFixes: Change the pip emissive colour and map from cream to saturated candle amber. The pip core is still #E7CCA9 (S 0.27) and the median #E5C59B (S 0.32). Target a core near #F3BE65 to #FFD848 with S of at least 0.55 after tone mapping, keeping the new halo. If the tone mapper desaturates it, raise the map saturation rather than the intensity.

Darken the inner well walls from the current pale grey-mauve (#847069, S 0.20, relL about 0.17, on 4 of 6 lineup dice) to dark brass or warm black near #231D1A, so the recess reads as panel 4's dark bevelled lip instead of a grey inset.

Give the brass value range and polish. Hue-masked relL still spans only about 0.12 to 0.24 with a mustard-olive median #85692E (V 0.52). Lift the lit midtone toward #DEC16A, add edge wear and cavity darkening so relL spans about 0.08 to 0.5, and check whether the environment or probe lighting, not the material, is what keeps it dull in the engine.

Make the pip cups read. Across the disc edge the minimum relL is 0.127 with no dark rim. Add a thin dark rim or an inner shadow ring (relL under 0.05) at the cup lip, or deepen the cup so the occlusion is visible at play distance.
independentScore.method: Independent reviewer (did not build the asset). I read the dice and palette sections of docs/art-bible.md and the previous independentScore in assets-source/dice/brass-d6/provenance.json, and I did not open any author status or self-score file in /tmp. Primary evidence was the in-engine stills of commit 68eca00 through the runtime loader (Apple M4, ANGLE Metal): docs/verification/p5-dice-brass-d6.jpg and p5-dice-brass-d6-lineup.jpg, both 960x640, cropped and upscaled 2x to 4x for inspection. The Blender review sheet assets-source/dice/dice.review-sheet.jpg was viewed for context only. The reference was L-board-1.png panel 4, cropped at (60,956)-(750,1490). Measurements used Pillow and NumPy under python3 -I: median sRGB in fixed crop boxes, hue-masked brass (H38 to 60, S above 0.3, cross-checked at S above 0.45), pixel scans across frames, rails and walls, and ring or distance profiles around pips and numerals. Pips were segmented at relL above 0.45, walnut at relL below 0.10 with H8 to 35 and S above 0.35, and the glow halo was measured in elliptical rings normalised to the centre pip's half-widths. Contrast ratios are WCAG (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) on relative luminance. The deltas against the previous score are approximate, because these stills now bind the glow pages as the runtime does and the earlier stills showed less emission. All evidence is desktop only, with no headset capture. Date 2026-11-16.
